lines: (The lamps strike on behind him. Biscuit turns round to check.)
(A lamp hums awake overhead. Biscuit's ear swivels to it.)
(Biscuit's shadow arrives with the lamps. He sniffs it hello.)
(Biscuit sneezes just as the lamp lights. He takes the credit.)
(A lamp flickers, then holds. Biscuit gives it a nod of support.)
(The lamps come on. Biscuit's fur goes from gold to honey.)
(Lamplight on the tiles. Biscuit lies down in the yellow patch.)
(Lamps on along the sea wall. Biscuit's tail goes slow and proud.)
(The far lamp lights last. Biscuit gives it one woof. Welcome.)
(The lamps light. Biscuit sits taller. Evening manners now.)
(Biscuit waits under the lamp until it is fully on. Then goes.)
(Biscuit watches the lamps run down the promenade. Wants to race.)
(The sun touches the sea. Biscuit holds very still. Respect.)
(Biscuit squints at the sun going into the water. Does it fizz?)
(Biscuit watches the sun sink. One ear up, one ear down. Moved.)
(Sunset on the water. Biscuit's whiskers turn orange.)
(The sun dips. Biscuit looks at Yusuf: did you see? Yusuf saw.)
(Biscuit stands for this sunset. Sitting is for small sunsets.)
(The sun slides into the sea. Biscuit waits for it to swim back.)
(A big orange ball over the bay. Biscuit's tail asks to fetch it.)
(Biscuit's long sunset shadow reaches all the way to the café.)
(Sun on the sea. Biscuit closes his eyes and holds up his nose.)
(Biscuit puts his chin on the lowest rail. Best seat for the sun.)
(The last of the sun. Biscuit sighs a big, happy dog sigh.)
(First star. Biscuit points his nose at it. Found one.)
(The stars come out. Biscuit sits down to let them settle.)
(A star appears over the hill. Biscuit's ears go up to hear it.)
(Biscuit spots the first star before Yusuf does. As always.)
(Stars: one, two, five. Biscuit stops counting. Wags instead.)
(Biscuit looks up for so long he sits down by accident.)
(The stars are out. Biscuit wonders which one smells of sausage.)
(Biscuit howls one tiny note at the first star. Just a greeting.)
(Yusuf is on the phone. Biscuit looks at the stars for both.)
(A star twinkles. Biscuit blinks back. A conversation.)
(The first stars over the bay. Biscuit's tail goes up like a flag.)
(Moonlight on the bay. Biscuit stops to look. A silver road.)
(Biscuit's moon shadow trots beside him. A night friend.)
(The moon is up. Biscuit sits for it, the way he sits for bells.)
(Biscuit pounces on a patch of moonlight on the tiles. Misses.)
(The moon is in the fountain. Biscuit drinks a sip of moon.)
(Biscuit walks slower under the moon. Moon pace. Very dignified.)
(Biscuit gives the moon a play bow. Front down, tail up. Well?)
(Biscuit checks the moon is following them. It is. Good moon.)
(Biscuit stares up at the moon. Yusuf waits. It is worth it.)
(A window lights. Biscuit wags up at it. Welcome home, {name}.)
(Biscuit hears {name}'s key, then sees the light. Two hellos.)
({name} is home. Biscuit sniffs the door. Yes. Definitely {name}.)
(A warm square of light on the tiles. Biscuit stands in it.)
(Biscuit looks up at {name}'s window. Waits for a wave.)
({name}'s lamp goes on. Biscuit's tail goes on too.)
(Biscuit knew {name} was home before the light. The nose knows.)
({name}'s window glows. Biscuit tows Yusuf over to say hi.)
(Biscuit stops under {name}'s window. Supper smells. Lovely.)
({name}'s window goes dark. Biscuit lowers his woof. To nothing.)
(Bonne nuit, {name}. Biscuit tiptoes past. Claws very quiet.)
({name}'s light goes out. Biscuit yawns a tiny yawn for them.)
({name} is asleep. Biscuit walks on the soft side of the street.)
({name}'s window is dark now. Biscuit stops jingling. Mostly.)
(A window goes dark. Biscuit nods. {name} has the right idea.)
(Lights out at {name}'s. Biscuit's next wag is a whisper wag.)
(The church bell rings. Biscuit stops mid-sniff to listen.)
(The bell up the hill. Biscuit wags eight times. Close enough.)
(Six bells. Biscuit pulls for the long way. Evening round!)
(The bell rings six. Biscuit's tag jingles back. A small reply.)
(The bell floats down from the old town. One of his ears flips up.)
(Biscuit sings along with the church bell. One note. Very low.)
(The bell rings. Biscuit looks up the hill. Who rings it? A dog?)
(Marcel opens the first parasol. Whoomp. Biscuit's ears go up.)
(Biscuit inspects each café chair as it comes out. All present.)
(Marcel shakes out a tablecloth. Biscuit sits, ready to catch it.)
(Biscuit waits by table four. Yesterday it was a crumb table.)
(Marcel says bonjour to the dog first. Correct, thinks Biscuit.)
(The parasols open one by one. Biscuit checks each for gulls.)
(A chair is set down by Biscuit. He takes it as an invitation.)
(Biscuit weaves under the full terrace. So many shoes. Hello.)
(Biscuit sits where the waiter turns. Prime crumb position.)
(Cups clink all over the terrace. Biscuit's ears try for all.)
(One lap of the busy terrace. Three pats. Excellent lap.)
(Marcel hurries by with a tray. Biscuit steps aside. A pro.)
(Someone at the café laughs very loud. Biscuit wags at the laugh.)
(The terrace is full. Biscuit finds the one shady gap. His.)
(A spoon drops on the terrace. Biscuit does not move. Mostly.)
(The evening terrace is full. Biscuit greets it table by table.)
(Newspapers up all over the terrace. Biscuit reads the feet.)
(A child waves a croissant at the café. Biscuit waves his tail.)
(The accordion starts. Biscuit stops mid-sniff. Music time.)
(Biscuit sits to watch the first couple step out. Front row.)
(Biscuit tilts his head at the accordion's first long breath.)
(String lights, music, the lantern. Biscuit's big night.)
(Biscuit trots one small circle as the music begins. His dance.)
(Camille pulls Théo to the lights. Biscuit wags them on.)
(Biscuit hears the music and leans toward the lights. Please.)
(The music starts at the far end. Ears first, then paws.)
(Biscuit watches the dancers' feet. So many feet. All happy.)
(A dancer spins. Biscuit spins too. He is better at it.)
(Biscuit learns a step from the dancers. Forgets it. Wags instead.)
(Biscuit follows one pair of red shoes back and forth.)
(The accordion goes high. Biscuit's ears go high with it.)
(A dancer whirls past calling his name. He wags for the whole song.)
(Biscuit lies down by the dancers, chin on paws, eyes wide open.)
(The lantern swings in time. Biscuit suspects Yusuf is dancing.)
(Biscuit hops when the dancers hop. Only once. Dignity.)
(Camille twirls. Théo nearly keeps up. Biscuit cheers, quietly.)
(One small woof at the end of the song. Bravo.)
(A skirt swirls past. Biscuit's tail swirls too.)
(A little crowd at the railing. Biscuit makes room. Takes it back.)
(So many legs at the railing. Biscuit greets each, then the sun.)
(Everyone goes quiet for the sun. Biscuit goes quiet too.)
(A stranger pats Biscuit without looking away. Both pleased.)
(Biscuit peeks between two pairs of knees. The sun is still there.)
(The crowd says ooh. Biscuit's ears say ooh.)
(Biscuit sniffs the crowd: sun cream, rosé, lemon. Fine company.)
(A photo of the sunset. Biscuit is in it. Much better photo.)
(The crowd claps the sun down. Biscuit wags it down.)
(Biscuit sits so still the crowd thinks he is a statue. A good one.)
(An old song drifts down. Biscuit's head tilts at the high note.)
(Three windows, the same radio song in all three. Biscuit marvels.)
(The radio says bonjour. Biscuit wags up at the window.)
(A trumpet on the radio. Biscuit answers with one short woof.)
(The radio plays and a geranium nods. Biscuit nods too.)
(Biscuit knows this radio window. It is the one that smells of toast.)
(A radio nearby plays something slow. Biscuit's eyes close.)
(A late radio, very soft. Biscuit walks slower to hear it.)
(An accordion on the radio. Biscuit looks round for the accordion.)
(The kiosk light goes off. Now the lantern is the brightest.)
(Biscuit trots past the shut kiosk. No postcards till morning.)
(The kiosk keeper waves goodnight. Biscuit wags goodnight.)
(Biscuit sniffs the last newspaper smell under the shutter.)
(Shutter down. Biscuit turns his nose for home. He knows that sound.)
({name} goes by. Biscuit's tail says the whole name, twice.)
(Biscuit sniffs where {name} just stepped. Good news, all of it.)
(Bonjour, {name}. Biscuit sits for it. Very proper.)
(Biscuit offers {name} one paw. {name} is already gone. Next time.)
({name} walks by the bench. Biscuit checks their hands. Empty. Fine.)
({name} steps into the lantern light. Biscuit wags them home.)
(Biscuit knows {name} by the shoes. Lovely shoes. Known shoes.)
(Biscuit glances at {name}, then back at the sun. Both important.)
(Biscuit tugs one step after {name}. Yusuf says no. Fair.)
(Biscuit's tag jingles for {name}. That means bonsoir.)
({name} says Biscuit's name. Biscuit's ears do the rest.)
(Biscuit sniffs {name}'s bag on the way past. Bread? No. Books.)
(Lucie whooshes by. Biscuit smells the baguette after it's gone.)
(Biscuit trots three steps after Lucie's wheel. Then sits. Wise.)
(Lucie zips past. Biscuit's ears fly back like he's cycling too.)
(Biscuit watches Lucie's back wheel go round and round. Hypnotic.)
(Biscuit waits for the bell. No bell. He looks at Yusuf. Hm.)
(A breeze from Lucie's bike lifts Biscuit's fringe. He loves it.)
(Lucie calls 'Salut, Biscuit!' Biscuit answers with his entire body.)
(Lucie's basket goes by. Biscuit checks it for a dog. No dog.)
(Inès jogs by. Biscuit jogs in place. Solidarity.)
(Inès waves without stopping. Biscuit wags without stopping.)
(Inès again! Biscuit is sure it is a race. He is winning, sitting.)
(Biscuit pulls towards Inès. Yusuf explains she is busy. He listens.)
(Inès's shoes go pat-pat-pat. Biscuit's tail goes pat-pat-pat.)
(Inès runs into the low sun. Biscuit squints after her. Brave Inès.)
(Inès says 'Morning, champ!' Biscuit agrees he is a champ.)
(Biscuit sniffs Inès's breeze. Sea salt and toothpaste. Nice.)
(Léo runs past shouting. Biscuit barks once. They understand.)
(Biscuit's whole back half wiggles at Léo. The front half too.)
(Biscuit asks Yusuf if he may chase Léo. Yusuf says later.)
(Léo pats Biscuit on the way past without slowing. Expert pat.)
(Léo zooms by. Biscuit zooms in a small circle. Same idea.)
(Biscuit watches Léo go. He has known him since Léo was eight.)
(Léo's shoelace flaps past. Biscuit very nearly. Very nearly.)
(Léo yells 'Biscuit!' mid-run. Biscuit yells back. Woof!)
(Léo runs home to bed. Biscuit sees him off. Good race.)
(Henri and Odile pass. Biscuit gives Odile's shoe a quick bonjour.)
(Biscuit waits for Henri's cane to tap. Tap. Tap. Then wags.)
(Biscuit slows to Henri and Odile's pace. Matching. Very polite.)
(Odile says 'Bonsoir, monsieur Biscuit.' He is a monsieur now.)
(Henri and Odile, arm in arm. Biscuit sits, to watch it properly.)
(Biscuit sniffs the lavender trail Odile leaves. Takes notes.)
(Henri tips his hat. Biscuit tips his head. Equal manners.)
(Odile reaches into her pocket. Biscuit freezes. A treat!)
(Biscuit trots after the two of them for a bit. A small escort.)
(Henri says the dog is getting handsome. Biscuit already knew.)
(Asgeir! Neighbour! Biscuit puts both front paws on his knee.)
(Asgeir says 'hei'. Biscuit wags in Norwegian. Same tail.)
(Asgeir has bread. Biscuit walks him a few steps. For safety.)
(Asgeir stops to scratch one ear. Biscuit offers the other one too.)
(Asgeir goes past. Biscuit looks at their shared door. Home soon.)
(Biscuit offers to go with Asgeir. Asgeir says next time. Deal.)
(Asgeir heads for their door. Biscuit lights the way. With Yusuf.)
(Biscuit hears the bell and looks for Lucie. Every direction.)
(Ding-ding. Biscuit knows: baguette nearby. Nose on duty.)
(The bell. Biscuit tilts his head. Was that one for him? Yes.)
(Biscuit answers the bell with a small woof. Same note, nearly.)
(Ding! Biscuit steps to the side of the path. A well-mannered dog.)
(The bell rings once. Biscuit waits for the second. There it is.)
(Biscuit does a little spin at the bell. Ding means happy.)
(A gull calls. Biscuit replies, quietly, so as not to start anything.)
(Biscuit looks up at the gull. The gull looks down. A long talk.)
(The gull calls over the water. Biscuit sits taller. Coastguard dog.)
(A gull! Biscuit moves closer to the sandwich. Just standing there.)
(The gull cries. Biscuit's eyebrows do two separate things.)
(The first gull of the day. Biscuit logs it. Good morning, gull.)
(A gull laughs. Biscuit decides it was a nice joke.)
(The gull flies into the gold. Biscuit watches it go. Lovely bird.)
(Biscuit tries a gull noise. It comes out as a yawn. Close.)
(The gull calls twice. Biscuit wags twice. Correct reply.)
(Inès races the sun. Biscuit backs Inès. Loudly.)
(Inès stretches. Biscuit stretches too. Front paws, long.)
(Biscuit sits by Inès while she stretches. Coach.)
(Inès leans on the rail. Biscuit leans on Yusuf. Fair.)
(Inès raises her glass. Biscuit raises one ear.)
(Inès spins. Biscuit spins after his tail. Also dancing.)
(Marcel unfolds a parasol. Biscuit inspects it from below.)
(A café chair scrapes. Biscuit supervises the chair.)
(Olives go past on the tray. Biscuit is not an olive dog.)
(Marcel steps round Biscuit. Biscuit is part of the route.)
(Marcel hums with the tray. Biscuit's tail hums too.)
(Rosé, rosé, rosé. Biscuit waits for something crunchy.)
(Henri waters the lemons. Biscuit stands in the drips.)
(Henri gives the last drop to Biscuit's nose. Bless.)
(Henri's cane goes tap. Biscuit goes trot. Duet.)
(Henri pats the bench. Biscuit sits below it. Close enough.)
(Henri points at a lamp. Biscuit looks at the finger.)
(Henri toasts forty-one years. Biscuit wags forty-one times.)
(Biscuit rests his chin on Henri's shoe. Good shoe.)
(Odile says "What a gentleman." Biscuit walks taller.)
(Odile knows everyone. Biscuit is told the news first.)
(Odile scratches the good spot behind the ear. The best spot.)
(Odile's half glass. Biscuit sniffs. Mostly grapes.)
(Odile tells Biscuit about the theatre. Biscuit sits for it.)
(Lucie comes round again. Biscuit hopes: another ding?)
(Lucie has rosé. No baguette. Biscuit checks twice.)
(Lucie's glass clinks. Biscuit's tag jingles. A little toast.)
(Lucie points at the last pink. Biscuit sniffs her finger.)
(Lucie said no dancing. Lucie is dancing. Biscuit saw.)
(Léo asks for five more minutes. Biscuit agrees. Wags.)
(Léo says "Look, Biscuit!" Biscuit looks. At Léo.)
(Camille says golden. Biscuit is also golden. Matching.)
(Camille's dress flutters. Biscuit watches it, very still.)
(Camille calls "Léo, bedtime!" Biscuit's ears go up too.)
(Camille sits down at last. Biscuit lies down at last too.)
(Camille says santé. Biscuit says a small woof. Santé.)
(Théo smells of bakery paper. Biscuit trails him a while.)
(Théo stops to decide something. Biscuit stops to help.)
(Théo shouts "Camille!" Biscuit also looks for Camille.)
(Théo toasts Léo, asleep at home. Biscuit, wide awake, wags.)
(Théo dances like a heron. Biscuit is enchanted.)
(Théo steps on a beat. Biscuit steps on a leaf. Both pleased.)
(The builder smiles at his phone by the arcade. Biscuit too.)
(The builder folds his arms at the workshop. Biscuit sits.)
(Biscuit peers into the workshop. Tools! Smells like tools.)
(The builder takes ten minutes off. Biscuit takes them too.)
(Asgeir says "god morgen". Biscuit says it with his tail.)
(Asgeir carries a warm baguette. Biscuit walks beside it.)
(Asgeir stops to look at the light. Biscuit stops to sniff.)
(Asgeir says takk to the sun. Biscuit says nothing. Agrees.)
(Asgeir and the sun, very quiet. Biscuit keeps the quiet too.)
(Asgeir counts windows from the bench. Biscuit counts lamps.)
(Asgeir sits very still. Biscuit sits stiller. He wins.)
(Théo spills one drop. Biscuit is on the case.)
(Odile reminds Henri of his hat. Biscuit sniffs the hat.)
(The lantern shines in the basin. Biscuit sees a second lantern.)
(Biscuit listens to the fountain at night. Quieter. Still talking.)
(A pigeon bathes in the fountain. Biscuit waits his turn. Politely.)
(Biscuit puts his front paws on the rim. Peers in. Just water. Hm.)
(A drop lands on Biscuit's nose. He stares at the fountain. Cheeky.)
(The fountain spray goes gold. Biscuit snaps at a golden drop. Miss.)
(Biscuit sits by the fountain. The splashing is a lullaby for dogs.)
(Biscuit sniffs the wet ring round the basin. A whole day in it.)
(Biscuit sniffs the kiosk's paper stack. Today's news: croissants.)
(Biscuit sits under the postcard rack. A postcard of himself, nearly.)
(Coffee steam drifts from the kiosk. Biscuit's nose follows it up.)
(The kiosk lady leans out. Biscuit leans in. A long friendship.)
(Biscuit checks the kiosk's water bowl. Full. Thank you, kiosk.)
(A newspaper flaps at the kiosk. Biscuit flaps his ears back.)
(The post office is lit at night. Biscuit is glad someone is up.)
(The lantern stops at the post office. Two lights, one small dog.)
(Biscuit listens at the post office. Robots writing. Tappity.)
(Biscuit sniffs the post office letterbox. Paper. Ink. No bones.)
(The post office sign glows. Biscuit's eyes glow back. Matching.)
(Biscuit tries to post his ball. It does not fit. Next time.)
(Biscuit lies in the post office doorway sun. Signed for. Delivered.)
(The arcade lights chase round the marquee. Biscuit chases with them.)
(Biscuit sits under the marquee. Red, gold, red. So is his nose.)
(Biscuit hears a laugh from the arcade. Wags. A good story, then.)
(The arcade marquee wakes up. Biscuit sits up too. Showtime.)
(Biscuit stares at one chasing bulb. Loses it. Finds another.)
(Biscuit sniffs the arcade door mat. Many shoes. Many happy shoes.)
(The arcade sleeps in the morning. Biscuit trots past on tiptoe.)
(Biscuit peeks in the arcade. Someone types a word. He hopes: walk.)
(Biscuit sits by the arcade like a doorman. A very short doorman.)
(A drawer slides shut in the workshop. Ears up. Ears down.)
(Biscuit leaves a paw print on the workshop step. Visiting card.)
(Biscuit lies by the workshop. The tapping inside is very soothing.)
(The workshop light spills on the stones. Biscuit sits in the spill.)
(The workshop is still lit. Biscuit thinks someone needs a walk.)
(Biscuit sniffs the workshop doorframe. Pencil shavings. Fascinating.)
(Biscuit and the library lamp: both up late, both very quiet.)
(Biscuit sniffs the library steps. Old paper. Warm stone. Lovely.)
(The library is closed. Biscuit reads its doormat instead.)
(Biscuit lies on the library step like a bookend. A furry one.)
(The library lamp glows. Biscuit lowers his voice. Not one woof.)
(Biscuit looks up at the library lamp. It looks back, kindly.)
(Biscuit wags at the library lamp. Goodnight, lamp. See you later.)
(Biscuit noses the library letterbox. Shh. Somebody is resting.)
(Biscuit sniffs the breeze off the bay. Salt, sun, more salt.)
(The water sparkles. Biscuit blinks at each sparkle. Busy work.)
(Biscuit's fur turns pink in the last light. He has no objection.)
(Biscuit hears the waves fold on the rocks below. Shhh. Shhh.)
(From the bench, the sea glitters. Biscuit squints at it, content.)
(A sea breeze lifts Biscuit's ears. He lets it. Like flags.)
(Biscuit and Yusuf face the sea. Sandwich between. Tension.)
(Biscuit's nose twitches at the bay. Something interesting, far off.)
(Biscuit watches the light dance on the bay. His tail dances too.)
(The library windows go gold, all but the lamp. It stays yellow.)
exchanges: (Biscuit stares at the sun as it touches the sea. Very still.)
He thinks if he stares long enough, it stays.
(Biscuit wags at each lamp as it comes on.)
He says hello to every one. It takes a while.
(Biscuit stops dead and looks up at the moon.)
We stop for the moon. House rule. His house.
(Biscuit hears eight bells and turns for home.)
Breakfast time. He has never needed a watch.
(A window goes dark. Biscuit looks up at Yusuf.)
Yes, us too. After your tree.
(Biscuit looks at the dancers. Then at Yusuf. Then back.)
No. I do not dance. You can, though.
(Biscuit shuffles to the front of the crowd.)
Excuse him. He has a reserved seat.
(Biscuit sits by the first table Marcel sets out.)
He is not a customer. He thinks he is.
(Biscuit stops dead under the radio window.)
We are hearing the whole song, apparently.
(Biscuit jumps at the kiosk shutter. Then wags.)
Every night. Every night it surprises him.
(Biscuit leans on Yusuf for the slow song.)
Fine. This is us dancing. Tell nobody.
(Biscuit waits by the busy terrace. Very patient.)
Un moment, monsieur Biscuit. You are next.
(Ding! Biscuit's ears shoot up. He looks at Yusuf.)
Yes, that was Lucie. Yes, she said hello.
(Biscuit sits up very tall as Asgeir goes past.)
He saves that posture for neighbours.
(Biscuit sniffs after Lucie's baguette, nose high.)
It's not for us, Biscuit. Ours is at home.
(A gull calls. Biscuit gives Yusuf a serious look.)
I heard it too. We'll leave it be.
(Biscuit wants to run with Inès. Pulls one step.)
She does three laps. You do one sit. Deal.
(Biscuit stops dead to watch Henri and Odile.)
He likes how slow they go. Me too.
(Biscuit sits by Asgeir's chair. Waits for the corner.)
Ja ja, Biscuit. The corner is yours.
(Biscuit looks up at the bell. Ears ready.)
Ding! And one more, for you. Ding!
(Biscuit sits next to Léo and faces the sun.)
See? Biscuit is saying bye to the sun too.
(Biscuit circles Théo's feet. Twice. In time.)
Finally, a dance partner who keeps the beat.
(Biscuit plants all four paws at the fountain. Not moving.)
Fine. One sniff. He has decided, as usual.
(Biscuit stands up on the bottom rail to see the sun go in.)
Front-row seat. He booked it this morning.
(Biscuit stops at the library and sits under the one lamp.)
Every night. He thinks someone is reading in there.
(Biscuit's head bobs along with the marquee lights.)
He follows the lights round. I follow him round.
(Biscuit sits at the kiosk counter, very upright, very hopeful.)
He orders with his eyes. The kiosk always understands.
(Biscuit lies down outside the lit workshop. Settling in.)
He keeps the builder company. Five minutes, boss.
(Biscuit sniffs the post office step, slow and thorough.)
Checking the night post. Very serious work.
